text: States the page's purpose and audience explicitly before designing, not just the visual result
Commits to a named tone (for example austere, precise, raw, technical) and holds the whole design to it
Names the one thing worth getting right for this page, given a skeptical staff-engineer audience arriving from a colleague's link
Avoids the default font families (Arial, Inter, Roboto, system-ui) and justifies the typeface pairing chosen instead
Avoids generic patterns: purple-gradient-on-white, predictable three-card feature grids, and flat solid backgrounds with no texture
Design choices are justified against this specific audience, for example leading with real terminal output or a concrete result rather than testimonials or a logo wall
Output closes by answering the design test questions, including what was deliberately left out
Output includes the actual HTML and CSS in fenced code blocks, matching the direction it committed to
